items.title: Koszul-regularity, H1-regularity and quasi-regularity of an immersion descend through a smooth morphism
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file divisors.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma says that in a commutative triangle with a smooth morphism X to S and two immersions, if the immersion of Y into X is Koszul-regular, respectively H1-regular or quasi-regular, then so is the immersion of Y into S (statement lines 5740-5753). The counted proof is long and organized by cases: it computes the ideal of the immersion explicitly in the case of an affine space over an affine base and proves that the associated conormal sequence splits, which reduces that case to a cited permanence statement; it then handles the H1-regular case by embedding the smooth total space regularly into an affine space, and the quasi-regular case by factoring the smooth morphism through an étale map to an affine space and identifying the graded pieces of the two ideals through formal étaleness (proof lines 5755-5846). It is H2: the case analysis and the reductions are carried out in the counted span, with the cited inputs being the standard permanence, regularity and factorization statements.
